alerts.name: SQL Server CPU Usage
alerts.description: SQL Server process CPU utilization is high
alerts.query: SELECT record.value('(./Record/SchedulerMonitorEvent/SystemHealth/ProcessUtilization)[1]', 'int') AS value FROM (SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(XML, record) AS record FROM sys.dm_os_ring_buffers WHERE ring_buffer_type = N'RING_BUFFER_SCHEDULER_MONITOR' ORDER BY timestamp DESC) AS x

alerts.name: OS CPU Usage
alerts.description: Total operating system CPU utilization is high
alerts.query: SELECT 100 - record.value('(./Record/SchedulerMonitorEvent/SystemHealth/SystemIdle)[1]', 'int') AS value FROM (SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(XML, record) AS record FROM sys.dm_os_ring_buffers WHERE ring_buffer_type = N'RING_BUFFER_SCHEDULER_MONITOR' ORDER BY timestamp DESC) AS x

alerts.name: Long-Running Query
alerts.description: A query has been running longer than the threshold
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(DATEDIFF(SECOND, start_time, GETDATE())) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE session_id > 50 AND start_time IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('running','suspended','runnable')

alerts.name: Excessive Recompilations
alerts.description: SQL recompilations per second, measured as the change in the cumulative Re-Compilations counter between two samples, exceed threshold
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%SQL Statistics%' AND counter_name = 'SQL Re-Compilations/sec'

alerts.name: Batch Requests Anomaly
alerts.description: Batch requests per second, measured as the change in the cumulative Batch Requests counter between two samples, deviate significantly from baseline
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%SQL Statistics%' AND counter_name = 'Batch Requests/sec'

alerts.name: I/O Stall Time
alerts.description: The worst combined read and write stall of any database file over a five second sample window, in milliseconds per I/O operation. Two readings of sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats are taken five seconds apart and the difference is divided by the operations that completed in between, so this is a current measurement and not the since-startup average that DMV holds. It reports the single worst file, not an average across files. The value is 0 when no such operation completed on any file during the window.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @s TABLE(dbid INT, fid INT, ops BIGINT, stall BIGINT); INSERT INTO @s SELECT database_id, file_id, num_of_reads + num_of_writes, io_stall FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL); WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:05'; SELECT ISNULL(MAX(CASE WHEN v.num_of_reads + num_of_writes - s.ops > 0 THEN (v.io_stall - s.stall) * 1.0 / (v.num_of_reads + num_of_writes - s.ops) END), 0) AS value FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL) AS v INNER JOIN @s AS s ON s.dbid = v.database_id AND s.fid = v.file_id;

alerts.name: Excessive Page Splits
alerts.description: Page splits per second, measured as the change in the cumulative Page Splits counter between two samples, are high, may indicate poor indexing or fill factor
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%Access Methods%' AND counter_name = 'Page Splits/sec'

alerts.name: Signal Wait Ratio
alerts.description: Share of total wait time that queries spend waiting for a CPU to become available rather than waiting for a resource. Cumulative since the last SQL Server restart, so it describes the server's normal rather than its last five minutes, and unlike a raw wait-millisecond total it does not grow with core count. Thresholds follow Erik Darling's sp_PerfCheck 2.8: above 30% is notable, above 50% CPU scheduling is the dominant problem. The idle-wait exclusion list is SQLTriage's own 84-type list, a superset of his 48 - his 2.8 list predates several modern idle waits such as SOS_WORK_DISPATCHER, which alone can be over 90% of raw wait time on an idle SQL 2019+ instance and would dilute the ratio to near zero.
alerts.query: SELECT CAST(SUM(signal_wait_time_ms) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(wait_time_ms), 0) AS decimal(9,2)) AS value FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats WHERE wait_type NOT IN (N'BROKER_EVENTHANDLER',N'BROKER_RECEIVE_WAITFOR',N'BROKER_TASK_STOP',N'BROKER_TO_FLUSH',N'BROKER_TRANSMITTER',N'CHECKPOINT_QUEUE',N'CHKPT',N'CLR_AUTO_EVENT',N'CLR_MANUAL_EVENT',N'CLR_SEMAPHORE',N'DBMIRRORING_CMD',N'DBMIRROR_DBM_EVENT',N'DBMIRROR_EVENTS_QUEUE',N'DBMIRROR_WORKER_QUEUE',N'DIRTY_PAGE_POLL',N'DISPATCHER_QUEUE_SEMAPHORE',N'EXECSYNC',N'FSAGENT',N'FT_IFTSHC_MUTEX',N'FT_IFTS_SCHEDULER_IDLE_WAIT',N'HADR_CLUSAPI_CALL',N'HADR_FILESTREAM_IOMGR_IOCOMPLETION',N'HADR_LOGCAPTURE_WAIT',N'HADR_NOTIFICATION_DEQUEUE',N'HADR_TIMER_TASK',N'HADR_WORK_QUEUE',N'KSOURCE_WAKEUP',N'LAZYWRITER_SLEEP',N'LOGMGR_QUEUE',N'MEMORY_ALLOCATION_EXT',N'ONDEMAND_TASK_QUEUE',N'PARALLEL_REDO_DRAIN_WORKER',N'PARALLEL_REDO_LOG_CAPTURE',N'PARALLEL_REDO_TRAN_LIST',N'PARALLEL_REDO_WORKER_SYNC',N'PARALLEL_REDO_WORKER_WAIT_WORK',N'POPULATE_LOCK_ORDINALS',N'PREEMPTIVE_OS_FLUSHFILEBUFFERS',N'PREEMPTIVE_XE_GETTARGETSTATE',N'PWAIT_ALL_COMPONENTS_INITIALIZED',N'PWAIT_DIRECTLOGCONSUMER_GETNEXT',N'PWAIT_EXTENSIBILITY_CLEANUP_TASK',N'QDS_ASYNC_QUEUE',N'QDS_CLEANUP_STALE_QUERIES_TASK_MAIN_LOOP_SLEEP',N'QDS_PERSIST_TASK_MAIN_LOOP_SLEEP',N'QDS_SHUTDOWN_QUEUE',N'REDO_THREAD_PENDING_WORK',N'REQUEST_FOR_DEADLOCK_SEARCH',N'RESOURCE_QUEUE',N'SERVER_IDLE_CHECK',N'SLEEP_BPOOL_FLUSH',N'SLEEP_BUFFERPOOL_HELPLW',N'SLEEP_DBSTARTUP',N'SLEEP_DCOMSTARTUP',N'SLEEP_DIAG',N'SLEEP_MASTERDBREADY',N'SLEEP_MASTERMDREADY',N'SLEEP_MASTERUPGRADED',N'SLEEP_MSDBSTARTUP',N'SLEEP_SYSTEMTASK',N'SLEEP_TASK',N'SLEEP_TEMPDBSHRINK',N'SLEEP_TEMPDBSTARTUP',N'SLEEP_WORKER',N'SLEEP_WORKSPACE_MANAGER',N'SNI_HTTP_ACCEPT',N'SOS_WORK_DISPATCHER',N'SP_SERVER_DIAGNOSTICS_SLEEP',N'SQLTRACE_BUFFER_FLUSH',N'SQLTRACE_INCREMENTAL_FLUSH_SLEEP',N'SQLTRACE_WAIT_ENTRIES',N'STARTUP_DEPENDENCY_MANAGER',N'VDI_CLIENT_OTHER',N'WAITFOR',N'WAITFOR_TASKSHUTDOWN',N'WAIT_FOR_RESULTS',N'WAIT_XTP_CKPT_CLOSE',N'WAIT_XTP_HOST_WAIT',N'WAIT_XTP_OFFLINE_CKPT_NEW_LOG',N'WAIT_XTP_RECOVERY',N'XE_DISPATCHER_JOIN',N'XE_DISPATCHER_WAIT',N'XE_LIVE_TARGET_TVF',N'XE_TIMER_EVENT') AND wait_time_ms > 0

alerts.name: SQL Server Response Time
alerts.description: Times a trivial query on a connection SQLTriage already holds, in milliseconds, leaving out login time. A slow answer points at the network or a busy server, and a stalled SQLTriage process reads slow too. It fires only after the time stays over a threshold for 2 minutes, and a failed probe shows Unknown.

alerts.name: Page Life Expectancy
alerts.description: PLE is low, indicating memory pressure and excessive physical reads
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%' AND counter_name = 'Page life expectancy'

alerts.name: Buffer Cache Hit Ratio
alerts.description: Buffer cache hit ratio is low, too many reads going to disk
alerts.query: SELECT CAST(a.cntr_value AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(b.cntr_value, 0) * 100 AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters a CROSS JOIN sys.dm_os_performance_counters b WHERE a.object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%' AND a.counter_name = 'Buffer cache hit ratio' AND b.object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%' AND b.counter_name = 'Buffer cache hit ratio base'

alerts.name: OS Memory Usage
alerts.description: Operating system physical memory usage is high
alerts.query: SELECT (total_physical_memory_kb - available_physical_memory_kb) * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_physical_memory_kb, 0) AS value FROM sys.dm_os_sys_memory

alerts.name: SQL Server Memory Usage
alerts.description: SQL Server is using a high percentage of its max configured memory
alerts.query: SELECT memory_utilization_percentage AS value FROM sys.dm_os_process_memory

alerts.name: OS Paging (Swapping)
alerts.description: Operating system is actively paging memory to disk, measured as the change in the cumulative Page reads counter between two samples
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%' AND counter_name = 'Page reads/sec'

alerts.name: Database Space Full
alerts.description: The fullest data file on the instance, as a percentage of the largest size that file is allowed to reach. Every accessible database is examined, not only master. The ceiling is the file's configured maximum size, or the free space left on its volume when the file may grow without a configured maximum, or the file's current size when autogrowth is off. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @f TABLE(dbid INT, fileid INT, dsid INT, used BIGINT, sz BIGINT, mx INT, gr INT, ft TINYINT); DECLARE @d SYSNAME, @s NVARCHAR(MAX); DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(name) = 1; OPEN c; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN SET @s = N'USE ' + QUOTENAME(@d) + N'; SELECT DB_ID(), file_id, data_space_id, CAST(FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') AS BIGINT), CAST(size AS BIGINT), max_size, growth, type FROM sys.database_files WHERE type IN (0,1) AND FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') IS NOT NULL;'; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @f EXEC sp_executesql @s; END TRY BEGIN CATCH END CATCH; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; END CLOSE c; DEALLOCATE c; SELECT MAX(CAST(f.used AS FLOAT) * 100.0 / NULLIF(CASE WHEN f.gr = 0 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) WHEN f.mx = -1 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 WHEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) < CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 THEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) ELSE CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 END, 0)) AS value FROM @f f OUTER APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(f.dbid, f.fileid) v WHERE f.ft = 0;

alerts.name: Transaction Log Full
alerts.description: The fullest transaction log file on the instance, as a percentage of the largest size that file is allowed to reach. Every accessible database is examined, not only master. The ceiling is the file's configured maximum size, or the free space left on its volume when the file may grow without a configured maximum, or the file's current size when autogrowth is off. A log sitting near 100 percent of its current size but free to grow is not counted as full. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @f TABLE(dbid INT, fileid INT, dsid INT, used BIGINT, sz BIGINT, mx INT, gr INT, ft TINYINT); DECLARE @d SYSNAME, @s NVARCHAR(MAX); DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(name) = 1; OPEN c; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN SET @s = N'USE ' + QUOTENAME(@d) + N'; SELECT DB_ID(), file_id, data_space_id, CAST(FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') AS BIGINT), CAST(size AS BIGINT), max_size, growth, type FROM sys.database_files WHERE type IN (0,1) AND FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') IS NOT NULL;'; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @f EXEC sp_executesql @s; END TRY BEGIN CATCH END CATCH; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; END CLOSE c; DEALLOCATE c; SELECT MAX(CAST(f.used AS FLOAT) * 100.0 / NULLIF(CASE WHEN f.gr = 0 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) WHEN f.mx = -1 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 WHEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) < CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 THEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) ELSE CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 END, 0)) AS value FROM @f f OUTER APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(f.dbid, f.fileid) v WHERE f.ft = 1;

alerts.name: Disk Space Low
alerts.description: Free space on the volume with the least free space of all volumes holding database files on this instance, in megabytes. Every file of every database is examined, not only the current database.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT MIN(v.available_bytes / 1048576) AS value FROM (SELECT DISTINCT database_id, file_id FROM sys.master_files) AS mf CROSS APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(mf.database_id, mf.file_id) AS v;

alerts.name: Data File Auto-Growth
alerts.description: A data file has auto-grown, which can cause performance issues
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.fn_xe_file_target_read_file('system_health*.xel', NULL, NULL, NULL) WHERE object_name = 'database_file_size_change' AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/data[@name="file_type"]/text)[1]','varchar(10)') = 'Data' AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/@timestamp)[1]','datetime2') > DATEADD(MINUTE, -5, SYSUTCDATETIME())

alerts.name: Log File Auto-Growth
alerts.description: A log file has auto-grown, may indicate missing log backups or large transactions
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.fn_xe_file_target_read_file('system_health*.xel', NULL, NULL, NULL) WHERE object_name = 'database_file_size_change' AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/data[@name="file_type"]/text)[1]','varchar(10)') = 'Log' AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/@timestamp)[1]','datetime2') > DATEADD(MINUTE, -5, SYSUTCDATETIME())

alerts.name: Virtual Log File Count
alerts.description: The highest virtual log file count of any accessible database's transaction log on this instance. Every accessible database is examined, not only master. Excessive VLFs degrade recovery and log operations. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT MAX(x.vlfs) AS value FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS vlfs FROM sys.databases AS d CROSS APPLY sys.dm_db_log_info(d.database_id) AS li WHERE d.state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(d.name) = 1 GROUP BY d.database_id) AS x;

alerts.name: Filegroup Space Full
alerts.description: The fullest filegroup on the instance, as a percentage of the largest combined size its data files are allowed to reach. Every accessible database is examined, not only master. The ceiling per file is its configured maximum size, or the free space left on its volume when it may grow without a configured maximum, or its current size when autogrowth is off. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @f TABLE(dbid INT, fileid INT, dsid INT, used BIGINT, sz BIGINT, mx INT, gr INT, ft TINYINT); DECLARE @d SYSNAME, @s NVARCHAR(MAX); DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(name) = 1; OPEN c; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN SET @s = N'USE ' + QUOTENAME(@d) + N'; SELECT DB_ID(), file_id, data_space_id, CAST(FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') AS BIGINT), CAST(size AS BIGINT), max_size, growth, type FROM sys.database_files WHERE type IN (0,1) AND FILEPROPERTY(name, ''SpaceUsed'') IS NOT NULL;'; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @f EXEC sp_executesql @s; END TRY BEGIN CATCH END CATCH; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; END CLOSE c; DEALLOCATE c; SELECT MAX(g.pct) AS value FROM (SELECT SUM(CAST(f.used AS FLOAT)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN f.gr = 0 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) WHEN f.mx = -1 THEN CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 WHEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) < CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 THEN CAST(f.mx AS FLOAT) ELSE CAST(f.sz AS FLOAT) + ISNULL(v.available_bytes, 0) / 8192.0 END), 0) AS pct FROM @f f OUTER APPLY sys.dm_os_volume_stats(f.dbid, f.fileid) v WHERE f.ft = 0 GROUP BY f.dbid, f.dsid) g;

alerts.name: Disk Read Latency
alerts.description: The worst read latency of any database file over a five second sample window, in milliseconds per read. Two readings of sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats are taken five seconds apart and the difference is divided by the operations that completed in between, so this is a current measurement and not the since-startup average that DMV holds. It reports the single worst file, not an average across files. The value is 0 when no such operation completed on any file during the window.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @s TABLE(dbid INT, fid INT, ops BIGINT, stall BIGINT); INSERT INTO @s SELECT database_id, file_id, num_of_reads, io_stall_read_ms FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL); WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:05'; SELECT ISNULL(MAX(CASE WHEN v.num_of_reads - s.ops > 0 THEN (v.io_stall_read_ms - s.stall) * 1.0 / (v.num_of_reads - s.ops) END), 0) AS value FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL) AS v INNER JOIN @s AS s ON s.dbid = v.database_id AND s.fid = v.file_id;

alerts.name: Disk Write Latency
alerts.description: The worst write latency of any database file over a five second sample window, in milliseconds per write. Two readings of sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats are taken five seconds apart and the difference is divided by the operations that completed in between, so this is a current measurement and not the since-startup average that DMV holds. It reports the single worst file, not an average across files. The value is 0 when no such operation completed on any file during the window.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @s TABLE(dbid INT, fid INT, ops BIGINT, stall BIGINT); INSERT INTO @s SELECT database_id, file_id, num_of_writes, io_stall_write_ms FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL); WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:05'; SELECT ISNULL(MAX(CASE WHEN v.num_of_writes - s.ops > 0 THEN (v.io_stall_write_ms - s.stall) * 1.0 / (v.num_of_writes - s.ops) END), 0) AS value FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL) AS v INNER JOIN @s AS s ON s.dbid = v.database_id AND s.fid = v.file_id;

alerts.name: TempDB Space Used
alerts.description: TempDB data file space usage is high
alerts.query: SELECT SUM(CAST(allocated_extent_page_count AS FLOAT)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CAST(total_page_count AS FLOAT)), 0) AS value FROM tempdb.sys.dm_db_file_space_usage

alerts.name: TempDB Contention
alerts.description: Tasks waiting at this instant on a tempdb allocation page latch (PFS, GAM or SGAM). Read from sys.dm_os_waiting_tasks and filtered to database 2 and to allocation page numbers, so page latch waits in user databases and on tempdb data pages are not counted. This is an instantaneous count of waiting tasks, not a wait time, and it is sampled once per evaluation, so contention that starts and clears between samples is not seen.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_os_waiting_tasks AS wt CROSS APPLY (SELECT TRY_CAST(PARSENAME(REPLACE(wt.resource_description, ':', '.'), 1) AS INT) AS pg) AS p WHERE wt.wait_type LIKE 'PAGELATCH[_]%' AND wt.resource_description LIKE '2:%' AND p.pg IS NOT NULL AND (p.pg = 1 OR p.pg % 8088 = 0 OR p.pg = 2 OR p.pg % 511232 = 0 OR p.pg = 3 OR p.pg % 511232 = 1);

alerts.name: TempDB Auto-Growth
alerts.description: TempDB has auto-grown, indicating potential sizing issue
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.fn_xe_file_target_read_file('system_health*.xel', NULL, NULL, NULL) WHERE object_name = 'database_file_size_change' AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/data[@name="database_id"]/value)[1]','int') = 2 AND CONVERT(XML, event_data).value('(event/@timestamp)[1]','datetime2') > DATEADD(MINUTE, -5, SYSUTCDATETIME())

alerts.name: TempDB Files Different Sizes
alerts.description: TempDB data files have different sizes, causing uneven round-robin allocation
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN MAX(size) > 0 THEN (MAX(size) - MIN(size)) * 100.0 / MAX(size) ELSE 0 END AS value FROM tempdb.sys.database_files WHERE type = 0

alerts.name: Version Store Size
alerts.description: TempDB version store is consuming significant space
alerts.query: SELECT SUM(version_store_reserved_page_count) * 8 / 1024 AS value FROM tempdb.sys.dm_db_file_space_usage

alerts.name: Deadlock Detected
alerts.description: One or more deadlocks detected in the system_health ring buffer in the last 5 minutes. The count is of xml_deadlock_report events in that window, read from the ring buffer, and it fires on the first one.
alerts.remediation: Review deadlock graph in Live > Deadlocks. Identify victim process and examine transaction order. Consider adding WITH (NOLOCK) hints or reordering table access to break the cycle.

alerts.name: Deadlock Rate
alerts.description: Deadlocks per minute, measured as the change in the cumulative Deadlocks counter between two samples, exceeds threshold
alerts.query: SELECT cntr_value AS value FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%Locks%' AND counter_name = 'Number of Deadlocks/sec' AND instance_name = '_Total'

alerts.name: Blocking Process
alerts.description: A session is being blocked for longer than the threshold
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(wait_time / 1000) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id > 0

alerts.name: Blocked Session Count
alerts.description: Number of currently blocked sessions exceeds threshold
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id > 0

alerts.name: Instance Unreachable
alerts.description: A connection to this SQL Server instance could not be opened. The check answers 1 for unreachable and 0 for reachable, so it fires the first time a connection fails and clears the first time one succeeds.
alerts.query: SELECT 1 AS value

alerts.name: Database Unavailable
alerts.description: A user database is not in ONLINE state
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.databases WHERE database_id > 4 AND state <> 0

alerts.name: SQL Agent Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Agent service is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Agent%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: SQL Agent Job Failed
alerts.description: A SQL Agent job has failed
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory h JOIN msdb.dbo.sysjobs j ON j.job_id = h.job_id WHERE h.step_id = 0 AND h.run_status = 0 AND msdb.dbo.agent_datetime(h.run_date, h.run_time) > DATEADD(MINUTE, -5, GETDATE())

alerts.name: SQL Agent Job Long Running
alerts.description: The elapsed run time of the longest currently running SQL Agent job, in seconds. This is a raw elapsed time. It is not compared against the job's own average duration: no baseline is computed for this alert.
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(DATEDIFF(SECOND, ja.start_execution_date, GETDATE())) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobactivity ja WHERE ja.start_execution_date IS NOT NULL AND ja.stop_execution_date IS NULL AND ja.session_id = (SELECT MAX(session_id) FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobactivity)

alerts.name: SQL Agent Job Completion
alerts.description: A SQL Agent job has completed (informational)
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory h WHERE h.step_id = 0 AND h.run_status = 1 AND msdb.dbo.agent_datetime(h.run_date, h.run_time) > DATEADD(MINUTE, -5, GETDATE())

alerts.name: Full-Text Search Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Full-Text Search service is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN FULLTEXTSERVICEPROPERTY('IsFullTextInstalled') = 1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Full-Text%' AND status = 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: DTC Service Stopped
alerts.description: Distributed Transaction Coordinator service is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%DTC%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: SQL Browser Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Browser service is not running (required for named instances)
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Browser%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: SSIS Service Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Integration Services is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Integration%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: Full Backup Overdue
alerts.description: A user database has not had a full backup within the threshold period
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(ISNULL(DATEDIFF(HOUR, b.backup_finish_date, GETDATE()), 9999)) AS value FROM sys.databases d LEFT JOIN msdb.dbo.backupset b ON d.name = b.database_name AND b.type = 'D' WHERE d.database_id > 4 AND d.state = 0 GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY value DESC

alerts.name: Differential Backup Overdue
alerts.description: A user database has not had a differential backup within the threshold period
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(ISNULL(DATEDIFF(HOUR, b.backup_finish_date, GETDATE()), 9999)) AS value FROM sys.databases d LEFT JOIN msdb.dbo.backupset b ON d.name = b.database_name AND b.type = 'I' WHERE d.database_id > 4 AND d.state = 0 AND d.recovery_model_desc <> 'SIMPLE' GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY value DESC

alerts.name: Log Backup Overdue
alerts.description: A database in FULL recovery has not had a log backup within the threshold period
alerts.query: SELECT MAX(ISNULL(DATEDIFF(MINUTE, b.backup_finish_date, GETDATE()), 99999)) AS value FROM sys.databases d LEFT JOIN msdb.dbo.backupset b ON d.name = b.database_name AND b.type = 'L' WHERE d.database_id > 4 AND d.state = 0 AND d.recovery_model_desc <> 'SIMPLE' GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY value DESC

alerts.name: Integrity Check Overdue
alerts.description: Hours since the last clean DBCC CHECKDB on the most overdue online user database, and a database never checked counts as overdue. On a build that does not report that date it runs DBCC DBINFO, which can refuse a login without sysadmin. A database whose date cannot be read is left out, and with none readable the alert reports that it cannot be evaluated.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @dbs TABLE (name sysname NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, last_good datetime NULL, tried bit NOT NULL); DECLARE @dbinfo TABLE (ParentObject nvarchar(255) NULL, [Object] nvarchar(255) NULL, Field nvarchar(255) NULL, [VALUE] nvarchar(4000) NULL); DECLARE @name sysname; INSERT INTO @dbs (name, last_good, tried) SELECT d.name, CONVERT(datetime, DATABASEPROPERTYEX(d.name, 'LastGoodCheckDbTime')), 0 FROM sys.databases AS d WHERE d.database_id > 4 AND d.state = 0; WHILE 1 = 1 BEGIN SET @name = NULL; SELECT TOP (1) @name = name FROM @dbs WHERE last_good IS NULL AND tried = 0 ORDER BY name; IF @name IS NULL BREAK; UPDATE @dbs SET tried = 1 WHERE name = @name; DELETE FROM @dbinfo; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @dbinfo EXEC sys.sp_executesql N'DBCC DBINFO(@db) WITH TABLERESULTS, NO_INFOMSGS', N'@db sysname', @db = @name; UPDATE @dbs SET last_good = (SELECT TOP (1) TRY_CONVERT(datetime, [VALUE], 121) FROM @dbinfo WHERE Field = N'dbi_dbccLastKnownGood') WHERE name = @name; END TRY BEGIN CATCH SET @name = NULL; END CATCH END; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM @dbs) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM @dbs WHERE last_good IS NOT NULL) THROW 50001, N'SQLTriage could not read the date of the last clean DBCC CHECKDB for any online user database. This alert cannot tell how overdue an integrity check is.', 1; SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM @dbs) THEN (SELECT MAX(DATEDIFF(HOUR, last_good, GETDATE())) FROM @dbs) ELSE 0 END AS value;

alerts.name: AG Failover Detected
alerts.description: An Availability Group failover event has occurred
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_availability_group_states WHERE primary_recovery_health_desc <> 'ONLINE' OR secondary_recovery_health_desc <> 'ONLINE'

alerts.name: AG Replica Not Healthy
alerts.description: An Availability Group replica is not in a healthy state
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states WHERE connected_state_desc = 'DISCONNECTED' OR synchronization_health_desc <> 'HEALTHY'

alerts.name: AG Replication Falling Behind
alerts.description: Availability Group log send queue or redo queue is large
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT MAX(ISNULL(log_send_queue_size, 0) + ISNULL(redo_queue_size, 0)) / 1024 AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states WHERE is_local = 0

alerts.name: AG Estimated Data Loss
alerts.description: Estimated data loss for asynchronous AG replicas exceeds threshold
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT MAX(DATEDIFF(SECOND, last_hardened_time, GETDATE())) AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states WHERE is_local = 0 AND last_hardened_time IS NOT NULL

alerts.name: AG Redo Queue Size
alerts.description: Redo queue on a secondary replica is large, indicating apply lag
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT MAX(ISNULL(redo_queue_size, 0)) / 1024 AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states WHERE is_local = 0

alerts.name: AG Listener Offline
alerts.description: An Availability Group listener is offline
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.availability_group_listeners agl WHERE agl.listener_id NOT IN (SELECT ali.listener_id FROM sys.availability_group_listener_ip_addresses ali JOIN sys.availability_group_listeners agl2 ON agl2.listener_id = ali.listener_id JOIN sys.dm_tcp_listener_states tls ON ali.ip_address = tls.ip_address AND agl2.port = tls.port WHERE tls.state = 0)

alerts.name: Cluster Node Not Up
alerts.description: Nodes of this failover cluster instance that sys.dm_os_cluster_nodes does not report as up, counting down, paused and unknown but not a node mid-join. A standalone instance has no rows here and never fires. This does NOT detect that a failover has happened: the instance keeps no record of which node owned it before, so a completed failover is invisible from inside SQL Server. What is visible, and what this watches, is a cluster node that is not available to take the next one.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_os_cluster_nodes WHERE status NOT IN (0, 3)

alerts.name: Mirroring Status Change
alerts.description: Database mirroring state has changed from normal
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.database_mirroring WHERE mirroring_state IS NOT NULL AND mirroring_state <> 4

alerts.name: Error Log Entry (Sev >= 17)
alerts.description: A high-severity error has been logged in the SQL Server error log

alerts.name: Error Log Fatal Entry
alerts.description: A fatal error (severity >= 20) has been logged

alerts.name: Login Failure Detected
alerts.description: Failed login attempts detected in the error log

alerts.name: Configuration Change
alerts.description: A SQL Server configuration option has been changed
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.configurations WHERE value <> value_in_use

alerts.name: Database Page I/O Errors
alerts.description: Database pages SQL Server could not read because of an I/O error and which have not since been repaired or restored. Read from msdb.dbo.suspect_pages, counting event types 1, 2 and 3 (I/O error, bad checksum, torn page); pages already restored, repaired or deallocated are not counted. This does not count transient I/O errors that succeeded on retry (error 825), which SQL Server records in the error log and not in this table.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.suspect_pages WHERE event_type IN (1, 2, 3);

alerts.name: Index Fragmentation
alerts.description: Significant index fragmentation detected on large tables
alerts.query:
DECLARE @frag TABLE([value] MONEY)
INSERT INTO @frag
EXEC sp_MSforeachdb N'USE [?];SELECT MAX(avg_fragmentation_in_percent) AS value FROM sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats(DB_ID(), NULL, NULL, NULL, ''LIMITED'') WHERE page_count > 1000 AND avg_fragmentation_in_percent > 10'
SELECT MAX([value]) [value] FROM @frag

alerts.name: User Connections High
alerts.description: Open connections to this instance as a percentage of its 'user connections' limit. When that setting is 0, the default, the limit is 32,767. It fires only on its fixed thresholds, 80 and 90 percent as shipped, never on a learned baseline or trend.
alerts.query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS FLOAT) * 100.0 / CAST(ISNULL(NULLIF((SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS INT) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = N'user connections'), 0), 32767) AS FLOAT) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_connections

alerts.name: SQL Agent Job Duration Unusual
alerts.description: A SQL Agent job has run significantly longer or shorter than its baseline duration
alerts.query: SELECT ISNULL(MAX(ABS(DATEDIFF(SECOND, ja.start_execution_date, ja.stop_execution_date) - avg_duration) * 100.0 / NULLIF(avg_duration, 0)), 0) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobactivity ja JOIN msdb.dbo.sysjobs j ON ja.job_id = j.job_id CROSS APPLY (SELECT AVG(CAST(run_duration AS FLOAT)) AS avg_duration FROM (SELECT TOP 10 run_duration FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory WHERE job_id = j.job_id AND run_status = 1 ORDER BY instance_id DESC) h) med WHERE ja.start_execution_date IS NOT NULL AND ja.stop_execution_date IS NOT NULL AND ja.session_id = (SELECT MAX(session_id) FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobactivity WHERE job_id = j.job_id)

alerts.name: Page Verification Disabled
alerts.description: Databases have PAGE_VERIFY set to NONE, risking undetected corruption
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.databases WHERE database_id > 4 AND page_verify_option_desc = 'NONE'

alerts.name: SQL Analysis Services Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Analysis Services is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Analysis%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: SQL Reporting Services Stopped
alerts.description: SQL Server Reporting Services is not running
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.dm_server_services WHERE servicename LIKE '%Reporting%' AND status <> 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: AG Query Slowdown on Primary
alerts.description: Synchronous replication causes query slowdown on the primary replica
alerts.query:
IF SERVERPROPERTY('IsHadrEnabled') = 0 BEGIN SELECT 0 AS value; RETURN; END
SELECT MAX(ISNULL(DATEDIFF(MILLISECOND, last_commit_time, last_hardened_time), 0)) AS value FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states WHERE is_local = 1

alerts.name: AG Not Ready for Automatic Failover
alerts.description: Availability Group failover mode is automatic but no secondary replicas are configured for automatic failover
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.availability_groups ag WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.availability_replicas ar WHERE ar.group_id = ag.group_id AND ar.replica_server_name <> CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('ServerName') AS NVARCHAR(256)) AND ar.failover_mode_desc = 'AUTOMATIC')

alerts.name: SQL Server Process CPU Low
alerts.description: The SQL Server process's own share of CPU, as a percentage, from the most recent scheduler monitor ring buffer record. This is the SQL Server process only. It is not total processor utilization: the same record carries SystemIdle, from which total utilization would be derived, and the two differ whenever another process on the host is busy. A sustained low value may mean the instance is not doing the work it is expected to do.
alerts.query: SELECT record.value('(./Record/SchedulerMonitorEvent/SystemHealth/ProcessUtilization)[1]', 'int') AS value FROM (SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(XML, record) AS record FROM sys.dm_os_ring_buffers WHERE ring_buffer_type = N'RING_BUFFER_SCHEDULER_MONITOR' ORDER BY timestamp DESC) AS x

alerts.name: Failed Login Tracking XEvent Session
alerts.description: No Extended Events session named TrackFailedLogins exists on this instance, so failed logins are not being captured to one. The check answers 1 when the session is ABSENT and 0 when it is present, which is the direction that makes a missing session the alertable state. Shipped disabled: the session is not created by this product, so it is only worth watching where you have chosen to create it.
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.server_event_sessions WHERE name = 'TrackFailedLogins') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS value

alerts.name: Unencrypted TCP Connections
alerts.description: Client connections open right now over TCP with encryption off, counted from sys.dm_exec_connections. Internal connections (a client_net_address beginning '<') are not counted. This is a point-in-time count of open connections, not a total since startup.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_connections WHERE encrypt_option = 'FALSE' AND net_transport = 'TCP' AND client_net_address NOT LIKE '<%'

alerts.name: Windows Power Plan Not High Performance
alerts.description: Checks if Windows Power Plan is set to High Performance
alerts.query: EXEC xp_regread 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE', 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PowerUser\PowerSchemes', 'ActivePowerScheme'; -- Check for 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c (High Performance)

alerts.name: Database Mail Not Configured
alerts.description: Checks if Database Mail is configured for alert notifications
alerts.query: SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM msdb.dbo.sysmail_profile) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS value

alerts.name: High Risk Linked Servers
alerts.description: Linked servers with both RPC Out and Remote Login enabled, which lets a caller run procedures on the remote instance under the linked credential. The instance's own row in sys.servers is excluded: every SQL Server carries both flags on itself, so counting it would report a high-risk linked server on every server in the world.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.servers WHERE is_linked = 1 AND is_rpc_out_enabled = 1 AND is_remote_login_enabled = 1

alerts.name: PUBLIC Role Dangerous Permissions
alerts.description: Permissions on user objects granted to the public role, across every accessible database. Anything granted to public is granted to every user of that database. Microsoft's own shipped objects are excluded: a stock SQL Server grants public SELECT on spt_values, spt_monitor and the spt_fallback tables in every database, so counting those would report a finding on every server in the world. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @p TABLE(n INT); DECLARE @d SYSNAME, @s NVARCHAR(MAX); DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(name) = 1; OPEN c; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN SET @s = N'USE ' + QUOTENAME(@d) + N'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.database_permissions dp JOIN sys.database_principals dpr ON dp.grantee_principal_id = dpr.principal_id JOIN sys.objects o ON o.object_id = dp.major_id AND o.is_ms_shipped = 0 WHERE dpr.name = ''public'' AND dp.state_desc IN (''GRANT'', ''GRANT_WITH_GRANT_OPTION'') AND dp.permission_name IN (''SELECT'', ''INSERT'', ''UPDATE'', ''DELETE'', ''EXECUTE'', ''ALTER'', ''CONTROL'', ''TAKE OWNERSHIP'') AND dp.class = 1 AND dp.major_id > 0;'; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @p EXEC sp_executesql @s; END TRY BEGIN CATCH END CATCH; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; END CLOSE c; DEALLOCATE c; SELECT ISNULL(SUM(n), 0) AS value FROM @p;

alerts.name: Implicit Conversions in Expensive Cached Plans
alerts.description: The PERCENTAGE of this instance's most CPU-expensive cached plans whose plan XML carries a PlanAffectingConvert warning with ConvertIssue 'Seek Plan'. That is SQL Server itself reporting an implicit conversion that stopped it seeking an index. Read the denominator carefully: the scan is capped at the 50 most expensive plans, because reading every plan in a large cache costs seconds of CPU on each run, and the percentage is taken over the plans ACTUALLY SAMPLED, which is at most 50 and can be far fewer. On a quiet instance it is much fewer, so a single affected plan moves the number a long way. MEASURED 2026-08-28, both idle: 46 percent (23 of 50 sampled) and then 42 percent on the same SQL Server 2022 instance a while later, where all the affected plans belonged to a third-party monitoring database rather than to any application; and 0 percent (0 of 6 to 8 sampled) on a SQL Server 2017 instance. The band sits above the worse of those readings, with room for the drift between them, on purpose. That calibration rests on two instances only, so if your own healthy baseline sits higher, move the threshold and say why rather than living with an alert that is always on. A reading of 0 also means an empty plan cache, which has no expensive plans to be wrong about.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(qp.query_plan AS NVARCHAR(MAX)) LIKE '%ConvertIssue="Seek Plan"%' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) END AS value FROM (SELECT TOP (50) qs.plan_handle, SUM(qs.total_worker_time) AS cpu FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats qs GROUP BY qs.plan_handle ORDER BY cpu DESC) AS tp CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_query_plan(tp.plan_handle) qp

alerts.name: Orphaned SQL Agent Jobs
alerts.description: Enabled SQL Agent jobs whose owner SID no longer resolves to a login on this instance. The job stays in msdb and may fail to start.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobs j WHERE j.enabled = 1 AND SUSER_SNAME(j.owner_sid) IS NULL

alerts.name: Low Page Compression Success Rates
alerts.description: The share of page-compression attempts that succeeded, across every accessible database, since each database's operational counters were last reset (an instance restart, or the index being rebuilt). A low share means the row shapes are not compressing and the CPU spent attempting it is wasted. No reading is produced until at least 1000 attempts have been made instance-wide, because a handful of attempts says nothing. Databases that are offline, restoring, or not readable by the monitoring login are not included.
alerts.query: SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @c TABLE(att BIGINT, suc BIGINT); DECLARE @d SYSNAME, @s NVARCHAR(MAX); DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE state = 0 AND HAS_DBACCESS(name) = 1; OPEN c; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN SET @s = N'USE ' + QUOTENAME(@d) + N'; SELECT ISNULL(SUM(page_compression_attempt_count), 0), ISNULL(SUM(page_compression_success_count), 0) FROM sys.dm_db_index_operational_stats(DB_ID(), NULL, NULL, NULL);'; BEGIN TRY INSERT INTO @c EXEC sp_executesql @s; END TRY BEGIN CATCH END CATCH; FETCH NEXT FROM c INTO @d; END CLOSE c; DEALLOCATE c; SELECT CASE WHEN SUM(att) >= 1000 THEN CAST(SUM(suc) AS FLOAT) * 100.0 / SUM(att) END AS value FROM @c;

alerts.name: SQL Agent Jobs Without Failure Notifications
alerts.description: Enabled SQL Agent jobs that tell nobody when they fail. A job counts as covered when it has an email, net send or pager notification set to fire on failure (or always) and an operator assigned to receive it. A write to the Windows event log alone is not counted, because no person is notified by it.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobs j WHERE j.enabled = 1 AND NOT (j.notify_level_email IN (2, 3) AND ISNULL(j.notify_email_operator_id, 0) <> 0) AND NOT (j.notify_level_netsend IN (2, 3) AND ISNULL(j.notify_netsend_operator_id, 0) <> 0) AND NOT (j.notify_level_page IN (2, 3) AND ISNULL(j.notify_page_operator_id, 0) <> 0)

alerts.name: Auto Update Statistics Asynchronous
alerts.description: Databases with AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC on. Statistics updates run in the background, so the query that triggered one compiles against the old statistics instead of waiting.
alerts.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM sys.databases WHERE is_auto_update_stats_async_on = 1

alerts.name: Host Machine Unreachable
alerts.description: A connection to the SQL Server instance on this host could not be opened. Read the name literally at your peril: this runs the same connection test as Instance Unreachable and nothing else, so it cannot tell a down machine from a down SQL Server service, and the two alerts fire and clear together. It answers 1 for unreachable and 0 for reachable, so it fires on the first failed connection.
alerts.query: SELECT 1 AS value
